Every block here was read against the baseline on 2026-09-20 (review fixes + prose pass): rival-name rewrites made on purpose, approved punctuation/wording edits, and sentences that only look shorter because the rest sits in a nested bullet. No fact lost. Any block added to this list needs the same check.
detail: A library handles hashing, sessions/JWTs. OAuth flows while you store users in your Postgres/MySQL.
Alongside the newsletter itself it runs the Boosts ad network and paid subscriptions. It takes a 0% beehiiv cut of paid-subscription revenue (only Stripe's 2.9% + $0.30 applies).
As MoR it absorbs chargeback risk but can hold or review accounts. Day-to-day holds are rarely reported, yet transition risk is high.
Because the data models are defined by the team instead of fixed by Attio, follow-up rules can reference whatever fields that team created. The AI works against the same structure.
Connections are built against a developer API instead of picked from a prebuilt catalog. Incoming data maps into the custom data model.
Contacts and campaign data export easily via CSV/API. Your list isn't locked.
Delivers a full Postgres backend (database, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions) from one dashboard without stitching separate services together. It keeps the data in standard Postgres.

Enterprise SSO and SCIM are billed separately per connection ($125 each at the entry tier, and a connection needing both is billed twice). Costs add up as the number of enterprise customers grows instead of staying flat.
Free tier: 300 credits/month, custom domains, and HTTPS. Its free tier allows commercial use.

Frontend and full-stack JS/TS teams (especially Next.js users) wanting zero-config Git deploys, preview environments, and edge/serverless functions. Best fit: Next.js and modern frontend apps where developer experience, per-PR previews, and a global CDN matter more than raw infra control.
GDPR/data-ownership rules or principle demand analytics on infrastructure you control. Choose this when ownership and privacy outweigh convenience.

Hobby is free but ships hard caps (100GB bandwidth, 1M invocations, 4h Active CPU and 360 GB-hr memory per month). Hitting any one cap stops the project serving until the next month, not auto-billing overage.
It covers fundamentals, not deep reporting, a known tradeoff for Buffer's simplicity.
It runs as a managed identity layer instead of a library. The user store and auth flows live on Clerk's infrastructure and integrate through its Next.js/React SDKs.
Its defining feature: retroactive autocapture of every click, pageview, and form interaction. You can define events after the fact with no code changes or replays lost.

Its main advantage is open-source (MIT) data ownership. Self-hosting is free beyond infrastructure, AI is included in the base, and it positions as a self-hosted alternative to the big hosted suites for teams that can self-host.

Its main advantage is open-source (MIT) data ownership. Self-hosting is free beyond infrastructure, AI is included in the base, and it positions as a self-hosted alternative to the big hosted suites for teams that can self-host.
Its strength is visual automation at a low entry price (Core is $12/mo for 10,000 credits, formerly 'operations'). Complex, multi-branch scenarios are reachable on a modest budget.
Lock-in is low. It's framework-agnostic.
Native to the Stripe ecosystem and its APIs. Integrations run through Stripe's own platform instead of external connectors.
Newer than the incumbents but funded. Its codebase was open-sourced in 2024, which is a community hedge.
No per-dispute fee, but you only lose the disputed amount if you lose. Eligible sellers get free Chargeback Protection covering up to $250/month in qualifying disputes.
No persistent backend or provisioned database, and SSR support is clunkier, so the latest Next.js features tend to arrive late here.
Only 8 countries. Online rates on the free plan are at the high end of this group.
Own your list outright, escape per-subscriber pricing. With Ghost you get a strong editor plus native paid subscriptions, a Substack alternative for a founder willing to self-host.
Paid memberships require Publisher ($29/mo+, scaling with members). Marketing automation is light, and it is not a transactional-email tool.
Pipedrive has been in the sales CRM market a long time and is widely used. Its feature set and support base are settled instead of fast-changing.
Pipedrive is a pipeline CRM rather than a data vendor. You bring the contacts.

Relational database running standard PostgreSQL. Ordinary SQL, constraints and Postgres tooling all apply, with the pgvector extension available for storing and querying embeddings alongside application data, not in a separate vector service.
Self-hosted broadcasting. You own the list and the sending.
Self-serve onboarding with KYC handled via Stripe. Developer-friendly by design.
Setup is moderate because of the depth of its ticketing configuration. Migration is a standard import.
Ships with built-in organizations and multi-tenant primitives as part of the hosted service. Team and tenant structures are provided instead of modeled from scratch.
Slower than the fastest host here. Serverless cold starts run ~3s+, edge function cold starts ~28ms, and average TTFB ~90ms in 2026 benchmarks.
Smaller community and fewer public playbooks.
Solid acquisition toolkit, but there is no built-in discovery or referral network.
Subscription depth is narrow, and the toolset is aimed at simple digital-product billing instead of enterprise contracts.
Surface price is in line with this group, but the credit model changes the real cost.
The Agent works in billable 'checkpoints'. There is real code access, a built-in database, and one-click deploys (autoscale or reserved VM).

The cheapest integrated auth at scale for Supabase users. 100K MAU is included in the $25/mo Pro plan ($0.00325/MAU only above 100K), a fraction of per-user pricing at that scale, while keeping users in your own Postgres with RLS integration. Cost and database integration are its distinguishing points.
The data in Attio is first-party. Compliance rests with you.
You eat them directly, at ~$15 per dispute plus the lost amount. Assemble the evidence yourself.

You need broad integrations, landing pages, and multichannel marketing on a single well-known platform and want CRM, ads, and ecommerce under one roof instead of a pure email tool. Essentials from $13, Standard from $20 (500 contacts).
You want to start free, publish instantly, and tap network effects (recommendations, Notes, discovery) with no monthly fee. You keep ~$8.40 on a $10 sub after fees.

You've already formed and need equity managed properly. Carta Launch is free up to 25 stakeholders and $1M raised, then custom-quoted paid early-stage tiers (no public flat monthly price like "$599/mo"; standalone 409As from ~$3,500) as you grow.
